original_question: Let T1, ..., Tℓ be arbitrary invertible measure preserving transformations, and let p1, ..., pℓ be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Must every measurable set A of positive measure contain a pattern of the form A ∩ T1^{m+p1(n)} A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{m+pℓ(n)} A with positive measure for some m, n ∈ N?
target_in_paper: Section 5.3, Problem 21 (under the heading "Transformations that do not commute") in the 2016 arXiv version; the same question appears as Problem 18 on page 25 of the 2011 version. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core of the paper’s intended open problem: arbitrary invertible measure-preserving transformations (so no commutativity hypothesis), distinct polynomials with zero constant term, a measurable set A of positive measure, and the existence of m,n in N giving a positive-measure multiple intersection. It is clearly aiming at the multiple-recurrence question stated immediately after the pointwise-convergence theorem for averages involving the extra variable m+p_i(n). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
missing_details: The ambient object should be a probability space (X, 𝓧, μ), and A should be specified as a measurable set A ∈ 𝓧 with μ(A) > 0.
The transformations T1,...,Tℓ should be stated as maps Xi : X -> X acting on the same probability space; the paper does not assume they commute.
The official statement is written with preimages: μ(A ∩ T1^{-m-p1(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{-m-pℓ(n)}A) > 0. If one writes T_i^{m+p_i(n)}A instead, one must specify the convention for how T_i acts on sets.
To make the iterates well-defined, the polynomials should be described as integer-valued on integers (equivalently, in this context, polynomial iterates taking integer values), with p_i(0)=0.
The quantifiers should be fully explicit: for every A with μ(A) > 0, there exist m,n ∈ N such that the stated intersection has positive measure.

The draft does not indicate the nearby paper-context: this is the recurrence counterpart of the theorem on pointwise convergence of averages with shifts m+p_i(n), and the paper records known special cases immediately after the problem.
No extra hypotheses such as rational independence, degree restrictions, weak mixing, commutativity, nilpotency, or lower-bound conclusions of the form μ(A)^{ℓ+1}-ε belong in the official formulation.
refined_question: Let (X, 𝓧, μ) be a probability space, let T1,...,Tℓ : X -> X be invertible measure-preserving transformations, with no commutativity assumed, and let p1,...,pℓ : ℤ -> ℤ be distinct polynomials satisfying p_i(0)=0. Is it true that for every measurable set A ∈ 𝓧 with μ(A) > 0, there exist m,n ∈ ℕ such that μ(A ∩ T1^{-m-p1(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{-m-pℓ(n)}A) > 0? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation to your draft, and it is narrower than neighboring problems. It is not the commuting-transformations problem for intersective polynomials (Problem 18 in the 2016 version), nor the rationally-independent lower-bound problem (Problem 17), because your draft asks only for existence of a positive-measure intersection and allows arbitrary invertible transformations. The exact match is the noncommuting extra-variable recurrence problem stated immediately after the theorem asserting pointwise convergence of averages built from m+p_i(n). The surrounding paragraph also supplies two hidden pieces of scope: distinctness is necessary, and the problem is known in special cases such as rationally independent polynomials and weak-mixing systems. In the 2011 version of the same arXiv paper, the identical question is Problem 18 on page 25. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
